exp: x prints 00, y prints 50, z prints 12, giving 005012.

q: In C++, protected inheritance makes the public members of the base class ____ members of the derived class.
exp: Under protected inheritance both public and protected base members become protected.
Fields are resolved by reference type (A) while methods are dispatched on the object type (B): AB.

q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of encapsulation?
options: Control over how data is modified
Guaranteed faster execution of every program
Freedom to change internal implementation without affecting users
exp: Encapsulation improves safety and maintainability; it does not guarantee speed.

q: Which declaration creates a vector of 5 integers each initialised to 7?
exp: The constructor vector<int>(n, value) creates n copies of value.

q: Which keyword is used to place a Java class into a package?
exp: The package statement must be the first statement of the source file.

q:
Match the UML diagram with its use:
1. Class diagram  2. Sequence diagram  3. Use case diagram  4. Deployment diagram
P. Static structure of classes  Q. Order of messages between objects  R. Functional requirements and actors  S. Hardware nodes and software placed on them
exp: Class diagram shows structure, sequence diagram message order, use case diagram requirements, deployment diagram physical nodes.

q: A static initialisation block in a Java class is executed:
options: Once, when the class is loaded
Every time an object is created
Every time a static method is called
Only when the class is serialised
exp: static blocks run once at class initialisation time.
Static blocks run parent then child (1,4); then parent instance block and constructor (2,3), then child (5,6).

q: Why should the destructor of a polymorphic base class in C++ be declared virtual?
options: To ensure the derived destructor runs when an object is deleted through a base pointer
exp: Without a virtual destructor, deleting a derived object via a base pointer is undefined behaviour and skips the derived destructor.

q: If a Java class contains an abstract method, then the class must be:
exp: A class with at least one abstract method must itself be declared abstract.
m() runs first and its finally block prints F before the returned value 1 is printed.

q: Autoboxing in Java refers to:
options: Automatic conversion of a primitive value to its wrapper object
Automatic conversion of an object to a string
Packing several classes in a package
exp: For example int to Integer is done by the compiler automatically.
After p += 2, *p is 30 and *a is 10, so the result is 20.

q: Making the constructor of a C++ class private prevents:
options: Creating objects of the class from outside the class
exp: Only members or friends can then construct objects; this is used in the Singleton pattern.

q: Which relationship is best modelled using inheritance?
exp: Inheritance models an is-a relationship.
null matches both overloads; the compiler picks the most specific type, String.

q: Given that Shape is a Java interface, which statement causes a compile-time error?
exp: An interface cannot be instantiated directly; arrays of an interface type and null references are fine.

q: Which declaration uses an unbounded wildcard in Java generics?
exp: The ? symbol is the unbounded wildcard type argument.

q: What happens if run() is called directly on a Thread object instead of start()?
options: The body of run() executes in the calling thread like an ordinary method
exp: Only start() creates a new thread of execution; run() alone is a normal method call.

q: Which design pattern ensures that a class has only one instance and provides a global access point to it?
exp: Singleton restricts instantiation to a single object.

q: A C++ member function declared as void show() const; promises that it:
options: Will not modify the data members of the object
exp: A const member function cannot change the object's non-mutable data members.

q: The Liskov Substitution Principle states that:
options: Objects of a subclass should be usable wherever objects of the superclass are expected without breaking correctness
A class should depend on abstractions, not concrete classes
A class should have a single responsibility
Clients should not depend on interfaces they do not use
exp: LSP requires subtypes to be substitutable for their base types.
The overloaded + adds the x members: 3 + 4 = 7.

q: Two interfaces in Java declare the same default method and a class implements both. The code compiles only if:
options: The compiler is left to choose the first interface
One of the interfaces is declared final
exp: The conflict must be resolved by overriding the method in the implementing class.
A stack is LIFO; after popping 3 the top is 2.

q: Which statement about HashMap in Java is correct?
options: It does not allow null values
It maintains elements in sorted order
exp: HashMap permits one null key and many null values; it is unsynchronised and unordered.

q: In a UML class diagram, the multiplicity 1..* on an association end means:
exp: 1..* means at least one and possibly many.
Constructing x prints 1; passing x by value invokes the copy constructor, printing 2.

q: For class C : public A, public B, when an object of C is created the constructors execute in the order:
exp: Base classes are constructed in the order of their declaration in the derivation list, then the derived class.

q: In Java, an overriding method returning a subclass of the original return type is allowed. This feature is called:
exp: Since Java 5 an overriding method may narrow its return type; this is a covariant return type.

q: Which of the following is a marker interface in Java?
exp: Serializable declares no methods and only marks classes whose objects can be serialised.

q: A try-with-resources statement in Java requires the resource class to implement:
exp: Resources declared in the try header must implement AutoCloseable (or Closeable) so close() is called automatically.

q: The JIT (Just-In-Time) compiler of the JVM:
options: Converts frequently executed bytecode to native machine code at run time
Converts Java source code to bytecode
Removes unused classes from the heap
Checks bytecode for syntax errors before execution
exp: JIT compiles hot spots to native code at run time to improve speed.

q: CRC cards used in object-oriented design stand for:
exp: A CRC card lists a class, its responsibilities and the collaborating classes.
